title: Potential mechanism of Lactiflorin in treating ulcerative colitis via modulation of the PI3K/AKT pathway: a study integrating network analysis, bioinformatics analysis, and experimental evidence.
authors: Zhang, Mengjia; Li, Haotian; Yan, Ningjuan; Meng, Man; Su, Xiaolan; Liu, Yanjun; Chen, Runhua; Yang, Jianqin
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过网络药理学、分子对接和MD模拟探讨Lactiflorin经PI3K/AKT通路治疗溃疡性结肠炎，虽含蛋白-小分子对接模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与TF-DNA课题关联较弱。
abstract: This study is aimed at investigating the therapeutic effects and the relevant mechanisms of Lactiflorin in ulcerative colitis (UC) via a combination of various methodologies. The PI3K/AKT pathway identified through network pharmacology, and key pathways and therapeutic effects were validated by animal experiments, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations. The experimental verification was performed using an acute colitis model induced by 2.5% dextran sulfate sodium. This study further explored whether the key bioactive components could improve intestinal barrier integrity and alleviate ulcerative colitis by inhibiting the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. We performed hematoxylin and eosin staining, cytometric bead array, western blotting, and immunofluorescence. Network analysis identified 718 predicted drug targets, among which 264 were related to UC therapeutic targets. Animal experiments further confirmed the significant role of the key pathways and the effects of the pharmacological intervention. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations demonstrated Lactiflorin with a strong binding affinity to STAT3 (- 11.24 kcal/mol), AKT1 (- 15.61 kcal/mol), and PIK3R1 (- 11.95 kcal/mol). In vivo experiments, Lactiflorin improved the Disease Activity Index score and histopathological score in UC-modelled mice and suppressed the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines including IL‑23, IL‑12p70, IL‑17A, and IL‑1alpha. Western blot and immunofluorescence results revealed that Lactiflorin inhibited the expression of AKT, STAT3, and PI3K proteins (P < 0.01). These findings suggest that Lactiflorin exerts potential therapeutic effects against UC through PI3K/AKT pathway.
abstract_zh: 本研究旨在通过多种方法学相结合的方式，探讨芍药苷（Lactiflorin）在溃疡性结肠炎（ulcerative colitis, UC）中的治疗效果及其相关机制。通过网络药理学鉴定的PI3K/AKT通路，以及通过动物实验、分子对接和分子动力学模拟验证了关键通路和治疗效果。实验验证采用2.5%葡聚糖硫酸钠诱导的急性结肠炎模型进行。本研究进一步探讨了关键生物活性成分是否通过抑制PI3K/AKT信号通路来改善肠道屏障完整性并缓解溃疡性结肠炎。我们进行了苏木精-伊红染色、细胞微球阵列、蛋白质印迹和免疫荧光实验。网络分析鉴定出718个预测药物靶点，其中264个与UC治疗靶点相关。动物实验进一步证实了关键通路的重要作用及药物干预的效果。分子对接和动力学模拟表明，芍药苷与STAT3（-11.24 kcal/mol）、AKT1（-15.61 kcal/mol）和PIK3R1（-11.95 kcal/mol）具有强结合亲和力。在体内实验中，芍药苷改善了UC模型小鼠的疾病活动指数评分和组织病理学评分，并抑制了促炎细胞因子（包括IL-23、IL-12p70、IL-17A和IL-1α）的表达。蛋白质印迹和免疫荧光结果显示，芍药苷抑制了AKT、STAT3和PI3K蛋白的表达（P < 0.01）。这些发现表明，芍药苷通过PI3K/AKT通路对UC发挥潜在的治疗作用。
